frames.narration: Ana presses Play for her party of two. Her client has measured 18 ms to EU-West and 55 ms to EU-Central, and it sends one ticket for both players with those pings.
The API looks up the two ratings, 1,540 and 1,480. The party ticket takes the stronger rating plus a small penalty for the gap, so it is queued at 1,560 with a window of 25.
The ticket joins the ranked queue for EU-West, which is owned by one matchmaker shard through a lease. The shard keeps the queue sorted by rating in memory.

Nobody is within 25 points yet. Every second the shard widens the window by 10. After 8 seconds it is 105 points wide, and it finds another party of two at 1,640. The gap of 80 fits inside both windows, because the other party has waited longer and its own window is wider, so two teams of two can be formed.

The two parties become the two teams, and both tickets are marked as matched in one conditional write, so nothing else can take them. The shard asks the allocator for a server in EU-West for the four players.
The allocator claims a slot on a server from the warm pool with a single atomic write, so it is ready in milliseconds, with no waiting for a start. The pool is refilled in the background.
The address and a one-time token go back through the API to all four players, and Ana's client connects. The whole wait was 8 seconds and the worst ping in the match is 31 ms.

After the match, the result is sent once with the match id. The rating store applies it a single time and moves each rating by the surprise of the result, while the wait and the quality of the match are recorded for the dashboards.
